intro.title: Auth Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple authentication context to manage user login state across your Vue application. You'll learn how to use Vue's reactive system to create shared state that multiple components can access. The main technologies involved are Vue's reactive ref for state management and provide/inject for passing data through the component tree. By the end, you'll understand how to create a centralized auth store that tracks whether a user is logged in and make that information available to different parts of your app without prop drilling.
intro.usecase: Auth Context is a fundamental pattern for managing user authentication state across an entire Vue application, similar to how a dashboard or admin panel needs to know if a user is logged in to display personalized content or restrict access. For example, in an e-commerce site, the shopping cart icon, user profile menu, and checkout page all need immediate access to the current user's login status and details without prop-drilling through every component. This pattern is essential for building secure, maintainable applications where authentication state must be consistently available, such as in banking apps that show account balances only after login or SaaS platforms that conditionally render features based on user roles.
